title: Customizing zero modes with arbitrary spatial profiles
authors: Luohong Liu (刘烙宏), Qicheng Zhang (张起成), Shuaishuai Tong (童帅帅), and Chunyin Qiu (邱春印)
abstract:
Author(s): Luohong Liu (刘烙宏), Qicheng Zhang (张起成), Shuaishuai Tong (童帅帅), and Chunyin Qiu (邱春印)

Here, the authors demonstrate a universal head-body architecture that creates spectrally isolated zero modes with fully customizable spatial profiles in arbitrary lattices. Unidirectional couplings to a zero-energy head site enable independent amplitude and phase design, as visualized by the Tai Chi zero-mode pattern. Acoustic experiments realize diverse one- and two-dimensional morphologies, including “WHU” letters and phase vortices, underscoring the scheme’s robustness and practical versatility for on-demand wave-field engineering.

title: Conductivity of a non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid: Exact solution of the kinetic equation
authors: Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, and Dmitrii L. Maslov
abstract:
Author(s): Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, and Dmitrii L. Maslov

In a Fermi liquid, the quasiparticle scattering rate scales as T2, whereas the low-temperature correction to the residual resistivity can scale as T4, seemingly implying a strongly suppressed current-relaxation rate. The authors resolve this paradox here by solving the kinetic equation exactly for a disordered, non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid. They show that electron–electron collisions enter the conductivity through the quasiparticle scattering time itself, which controls the crossover between collisionless and hydrodynamic transport. The extra T2 factor arises because momentum conservation makes the change in the total velocity of two colliding electrons vanish on the Fermi surface, so current relaxation comes only from thermally excited states away from it. The electron–electron contribution to the dc conductivity nevertheless remains parametrically small throughout the Fermi-liquid regime. By extrapolating the result toward a z=3 quantum critical point, the authors further show that the renormalized quasiparticle scattering rate saturates the Planckian bound.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L291103] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026
